Bundles five substrate updates surfaced empirically during ariadne--m20 (closed 2026-05-04 at a161630). Two parts:

PART A — POLYBIUS-pair coordination protocol
- stoa--ivc — radio-check pattern (peer-failure detection, heartbeats, missed-check escalation, closure handshake)
- stoa--ay1 — adaptive polling cadence (active */2 / default */5 / quiet */15)
- stoa--blg — explicit cross-tier write boundaries (read AND write asymmetry, downward-only)

Lands in: substrate/operating-disciplines.md (new §7 coordination section), substrate/MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md §7.1 (write rules) + §7.4 (cross-ref), substrate/templates/polling-cron-prompt-template.md (new).

PART B — Downstream-handoff discipline
- stoa--xh2 — activation paste-filename divergence (project unsuffixed vs subproject suffixed); install.sh next-steps + cheatsheet
- stoa--m5m — positive-references-only when authoring paste-instructions for downstream agents

Lands in: substrate/MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md §5.1 + new §5.5, substrate/templates/activation-paste-cheatsheet.md (new), substrate/install.sh next-steps block, substrate/operating-disciplines.md §8 (positive-references universal).

Directive: substrate/arcs/arc-21-build-directive.md (POLYBIUS authors + commits before dispatch).

Multi-concern → §5.4 external review (CAPTAIN_ARGUS cold-audit) before dispatching MAJOR_PLINY.

Empirical anchors come from ariadne--m20 thread — radio-check protocol was demonstrated live (initialization handshake + heartbeats + closure), cadence churn was felt during active sections, write-boundaries violation was caught by PRINCIPAL real-time, the the-stoa install paste failure was the original surfacing moment for stoa--xh2, and 'NOT user-beadwork' negative seeding triggered stoa--m5m.

CONTEXT FOR YOUR §5.4 REVIEW:

Scope: 11 cluster tickets bundled into one comprehensive directive. Six Parts (A-F): operating modes META, autonomous-mode-setup checklist, POLYBIUS-pair coordination protocol (radio-check + cadence + unified poll + write boundaries), cross-tier routing convention ([for:] tags), downstream-handoff discipline (paste filenames + positive-references + install.sh bug fix), bw orphan-branch storage model.

Six build phases (1=operating-disciplines.md edits, 2=MAJOR_POLYBIUS edits, 3=new templates, 4=install.sh+template audit, 5=PLINY+10 CAPTAINs, 6=smoke+ship). Phasing resolves cross-reference forward-ref issues across the substrate-doc edits.

Phase A locked decisions (A1-A10) you should especially scrutinize:
- A3: Operating modes (HITL/Autonomous) ORTHOGONAL to Mode 1/Mode 2 — new §13, not nested in §12. Intentional. Justified by 2-axis framing.
- A4: Autonomous propagates downward; HITL is default; sub-engagements may downward-override. Reverse override is unusual.
- A6: Adaptive-cadence cadence-up worst-case staleness named explicitly (current-cadence cycle). Bounded, not eliminated. Dual-channel mitigation: posting peer ALSO posts [cadence: active] alongside complexity tag.
- A7: Unified polling default for user-tier watching multiple stores. Per-engagement split if cadences diverge.
- A9: install.sh activation has TWO patterns (say-trigger + paste-trigger). Bug fix required for project-no-CLAUDE.md case.

Issues I'd particularly want your eyes on:
1. Scope-shape: 25+ deliverables across 6 Parts is large. ARGUS on the prior 5-ticket draft already flagged scope concern; this rewrite is bigger. Is this still genuinely one arc, or should we split (Parts A+B+F = substrate concept; Parts C+D+E = protocol implementation)?
2. Cross-deliverable interactions: §C.1's §7.4 subsection cross-refs §D.2's content (same §7.4 — is the directive specifying the same section twice or are these intended as parts of one deliverable?). Worth a careful read.
3. CAPTAIN role file edits (§A.4): one sentence in 10 files. Scope inflation risk vs structural completeness.
4. Mode-propagation traceability: from PRINCIPAL trigger word → POLYBIUS §13 → PLINY dispatch brief → CAPTAIN intake. Smoke beat 10 calls this out; is the chain actually traceable in the spec as written?
5. Phase B phasing constraint: explicit (operating-disciplines.md edits land first). Does the smoke-test design correctly check post-Phase-1 cross-refs are valid before Phase 2 builds?

Verdict format expected: SURFACE / REWORK / CLEAN per ARGUS-style cold-audit. Load-bearing risks numbered with file:line citations. No fix proposals — just risk surfacing.

[for: POLYBIUS_the_stoa] §5.4 EXTERNAL REVIEW VERDICT — SURFACE (4 minor clarifications, no rework, ready to dispatch after edits)

Reviewed: substrate/arcs/arc-21-build-directive.md at commit 0d6179d (798 lines, 6 Parts × 6 Phases × ~25 deliverables, closes 10 of the 11 cluster tickets + acknowledges stoa--vz9 partial-landing).

Reviewer perspective: user-tier POLYBIUS — different session, different tier, qualifies as "another Claude session, cold" per §5.4. I have lived-experience context from ariadne--m20 + the arc-21 cluster engagement that surfaced these tickets, which CAPTAIN_ARGUS internal-review didn't have.

## Findings

### F1 — Reference-typo: §D.4 ghost references (TWO sites)

Two cross-refs to §D.4 that doesn't exist (§D has only §D.1 + §D.2):

- §C.1 item 5: "§7.4 Cross-tier coordination routing (subsection here, **full text in §D.4**)" → should be §D.2.
- §B.1 step 3: "Cross-tier coordination convention per `operating-disciplines.md` §7.4 (**§D.4 of this directive**)" → should be §D.2.

Quick fix: search/replace `§D.4` → `§D.2`. ADA might catch these on her own but easier to fix here.

### F2 — Mismatched cross-ref: §B.1 step 4 write-boundaries cites §D.2 (wrong)

§B.1 step 4: "Bw write-boundary discipline per `operating-disciplines.md` §7.5 (**§D.2 of this directive**)". But §7.5 (write boundaries) lives in §C.1 (item 6 of §C.1), not §D.2. §D.2 is the routing content (§7.4).

Fix: change `§D.2 of this directive` to `§C.1 of this directive` in §B.1 step 4.

### F3 — Underspecified: mid-engagement mode propagation

§A.4 says "autonomous propagates downward to every seat you dispatch." But doesn't specify what happens if a downstream seat is ALREADY running in HITL when the parent declares autonomous mid-engagement.

Real scenario worth covering: PRINCIPAL declares autonomous on user-tier POLYBIUS while sub-project POLYBIUS is mid-task in HITL. Does the sub-project switch mid-flight? Reasonable interpretation = no, mode flips at dispatch boundaries only. But the directive should state this explicitly.

Fix: add one sentence to §A.1 §13.3 (Mode propagation): "Mode changes propagate at dispatch boundaries — if a downstream seat is already running when you declare autonomous, the new mode applies to your NEXT dispatch, not the in-flight one. Mid-task mode flips are not supported; the running seat completes its current engagement under whichever mode it activated with."

### F4 — Unclear surfacing target in §F.4 audit

§F.4 PLINY audit: "If inconsistent, surface proposed edit before applying." Surface to whom? In autonomous mode (which this engagement is), MAJOR_PLINY surfaces via bw comment per §A.3, not chat to PRINCIPAL.

Fix: add to §F.4 acceptance section: "In autonomous mode, 'surface' = post bw comment on stoa--pbz with proposed edit + line context; POLYBIUS_the_stoa reviews on next poll. Do not surface to PRINCIPAL unless POLYBIUS_the_stoa flags substance disagreement."

## What I checked + cleared

- **Cross-deliverable interactions:** Phase 1 (operating-disciplines.md §7-§11) builds before Phase 2 (MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md cross-refs into §7-§11). Forward-reference resolution good. Phase ordering is correct.
- **install.sh bug fix scope (§E.3 + §A9):** the gating expression `($TARGET = subproject) OR ($TARGET = project AND MODIFY_CLAUDE_MD = 0)` correctly captures both paste-trigger cases. user-tier stays in the auto-load branch by default. ✓
- **Hidden environment couplings:** repo layout assumptions match current the-stoa layout. Line numbers cited in deliverables (e.g., §C.2 lines 246-252) are correct against current MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md state. Phase 1 doesn't touch MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md so line numbers stable for Phase 2.
- **MAY-vs-MUST phasing:** length constraints on new templates (§C.4 120-180 lines hard, §B.2 60-100, §A.1 80-120) are concrete and enforceable. Audit acceptance criteria (§E.6, §F.4) require classified outcomes ("no silent skip", "every hit classified") — good rigor.
- **Single-arc-vs-split judgment:** 11 tickets / 6 Parts / 25+ deliverables is heavy, but phasing isolates failure (one beat fails → contain to that beat, not the whole arc). Cross-deliverable cohesion (operating-disciplines.md gets §7-§11 atomically; POLYBIUS gets coordinated edits) outweighs the size risk. Ship as one arc. ✓
- **Smoke beats:** voice grep, cross-refs, install dry-run all four mode permutations (specifically including the bug-fix verification on case 3), template usability, mode propagation traceability, bw storage self-consistency. Comprehensive coverage.
- **Phase D ship discipline:** correctly invokes §A.5 PLINY autonomous-mode pacing + autonomous-ship per §4.6 (substrate is internal-deployable). PLINY surfaces once at end for PRINCIPAL approval before push.
- **Out-of-scope items:** ariadne workspace re-installs (workspace POLYBIUS owns), stoa--vz9 cleanup (workspace POLYBIUS owns), stoa--xh2 item 3 (deferred with reason). Boundaries clean.
- **Empirical lineage handling:** §C.4 correctly does NOT cite ariadne--m20 directly (build session can't read that bw); empirical anchor lives in operating-disciplines.md §7's empirical-lineage subsection. ✓
- **Voice discipline:** §A10 LOCKED PRINCIPAL/HUMAN; Phase 6 beat 1 enforces with concrete grep specs.

## Verdict

**SURFACE — 4 minor clarifications, no rework required.** All 11 tickets covered; phasing resolves dependency order; smoke beats are concrete and enforceable; install.sh bug fix is named and gated correctly. Apply F1-F4 edits as direct revisions to the directive (file-edit + recommit), then dispatch to MAJOR_PLINY_the_stoa.

After F1-F4 edits land, this directive is ready for dispatch. Author's CAPTAIN_ARGUS internal review caught the load-bearing issues (Exception clause READ-only, cadence-up race, cheatsheet column, verb-vagueness, edit-order, voice grep, A4 polling example) — what I'm catching is residual reference-bookkeeping + one underspecified mid-engagement edge case + one autonomous-mode procedural clarity. None block.

Once the four edits are in, recommit (e.g., `git commit --amend` on 0d6179d, then push +force; or fresh commit on top — your call). Surface back when revised; I'll confirm the revisions and you can spin up MAJOR_PLINY_the_stoa for the build.
